item.title: Install your tools
item.content:
This is the page where most people get stuck, so go slowly. You'll install the same tools working developers use: a runtime for JavaScript, version control, an editor, and the HAX command line. Pick your operating system tab and follow it top to bottom.

  • Read and watch: about 15 minutes
  • Do: about 1 hour (installs take time; let them run)
  • You make: a working terminal that prints version numbers
  • You need: a computer where you have admin rights (Chromebooks and locked lab machines won't work)
  • Support level: full

Read and watch

  • Watch this terminal primer first. You'll type commands on every page from now on.
  • Node.js and HAX setup guide: the long version of this page, by operating system.
  • Common issues: read it once now. It answers most problems before you have them.

Do: install, in this order

Install Git for Windows. Keep the defaults. It gives you Git Bash, the terminal to use for this course (PowerShell behaves differently from every example you'll find).

Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org and run it. Tick the box to install the extra tools if it asks.

Install VS Code. Open Extensions (the four squares on the left) and install lit-plugin and lit-html. They color the HTML and CSS inside your JavaScript.

Install GitHub Desktop and sign in. If git is new to you, use it: it shows what changed before you commit.

Close every terminal, open Git Bash, and run:

Every line should print a version number. command not found usually means you need to close and reopen the terminal, or restart.

Open Terminal (press Command and Space, type Terminal). The first command below installs Apple's command line tools, which include git.

Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org. If you already use Homebrew, brew install node works too.

Install VS Code and drag it into Applications. Open Extensions and install lit-plugin and lit-html.

Install GitHub Desktop and sign in.

If npm install --global says EACCES, see the permissions fix in the setup guide above instead of using sudo.

Install git with your package manager.

Follow the Linux instructions on nodejs.org. Using nvm keeps global installs out of system folders.

Install VS Code plus lit-plugin and lit-html. GitHub Desktop isn't official on Linux; the git command line is fine.

Do: browser add-ons

Chrome and Edge: install JSON Formatter. Firefox has one built in. Test it: open haxtheweb.org/site.json. You should see folding, colored data, not a wall of text. You'll read a lot of JSON in chapter 5.

Keep claude.ai pinned as a tab, or add Claude in Chrome if you're on a paid plan.

Stuck? Ask your study buddy

Use AI to explain, not to do the work for you. Paste your own code or error with the prompt, read the answer, then close the chat and type the fix yourself. If you can't explain the fix out loud, you don't own it yet.

You're done when

Journal it

Add a heading for this page to your dev journal (the public Gist you made in Start here) and answer in Markdown:

  • What broke during install, and how did you fix it? (Future you will thank you.)
  • Paste the version numbers you got.
